grh_e8a0cc1d83068230dea5.title: The Man Who Changed His Mind
paragraphs: Grocer Alex Johnson becomes furious when Dr. Christian quarantines his household after young Dickie contracts scarlet fever. Because Johnson runs a food store, the quarantine means he cannot simply live at home and continue working, and he declares that once the danger is past Christian will no longer be the family doctor. Weeks later the Johnson children play doctor in their backyard playhouse. They take real medicines from the house and give several pills and liquids to Dottie, then lock the playhouse as part of their game. When Christian learns what happened he breaks down the door, rushes the poisoned child to treatment and uses every antidote and stimulant he can while the family is being located. Johnson arrives still angry, believing Christian has interfered with his children yet again, only to discover the doctor is fighting to save his daughter. Dottie finally regains consciousness and passes the crisis. Faced with Christian's persistence and care despite having been dismissed, Johnson admits he was wrong, asks forgiveness and offers him a lifetime appointment as the Johnson family physician.

This [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]] broadcast aired on January 29, 1941. It is listed as episode 115 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Jean Hersholt, Helen Claire, [[person|don-maclaughlin|Don MacLaughlin]], Jeannie Elkins, and Warren Mills. Other credited names include Andre Baruch as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 25 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_e835affdc2557a84e4a9.title: Hit the Deck
paragraphs: Wealthy Lulu falls for sailor Mr. Smith, but his pride will not let him marry a woman with money, and he leaves determined to make his own way. grh_e8288f435235298b7995.title: Three Thousand Dollars
paragraphs: A sailor named Swenson wins three thousand dollars in a sweepstakes and happily plans to use it for the little farm he has dreamed of buying for his wife and children. His friend Tony, a hard-bitten deep-sea diver obsessed with money, dismisses that modest dream and soon accepts a dangerous dive for a share of a million dollars in sunken gold. Beneath the sea Tony hears the voice of a dead sailor calling to him; when the crew finally hauls up his line, Tony is gone and only a gold bar is tied where he should have been.
